spec: r3 §8.1 (L6a row: shared TTS + voice loop)
note: L6a adds no native build and no new npm dependency. The runtime digest checks (refuse on unpinned helper, at every synth/play call) are implemented and unit-covered, but the TTS helper has never been measured and the playback helper digest is host-only: until every digest and trace below is real, this receipt stays blocked, never claimed. No audio file is written by L6a at any point: espeak-ng renders to stdout and aplay consumes stdin, with bounded RAM buffers only.

toolchain.testImage: node:24-bookworm-slim (tag only; image digest not pinned — no lane exposes it, ad-hoc docker inspection is forbidden)
toolchain.nodeGyp: never invoked in live-speech install, build, test, synth or playback paths
toolchain.nativeBuild: none — no native module on the L6a path; faster-whisper-ts stays an optional L3 peer

packageDependencies.note: Zero runtime dependencies: tts-registry/playback/voice-loop import only node:child_process, node:crypto, node:fs, node:os, node:path and node builtins (plus an L1c type import).

aplay.hostDigestScope: measured on the Ubuntu qualification host — byte-identical to the vetted arecord build (dual alsa-utils binary, verified with cmp); NOT the node:24-bookworm-slim image, which ships no alsa-utils
aplay.imageDigest: missing — blocked: no lane provisions aplay inside the pinned image
aplay.license: GPL-2 (separate native executable, subprocess aggregation — same treatment as the L4 arecord binary)
aplay.invocation: aplay [-D <device>] with the WAV on stdin, header-autodetected (explicit argv, shell:false; SIGTERM then SIGKILL at 100 ms + reap on cancel, bounded by the 150 ms gate)
aplay.runtimeEnforcement: AplayPlayback.play resolves the binary to an absolute path, hashes it, and refuses anything outside APLAY_SHA256_PINS plus constructor/APLAY_DIGESTS allowlist (PlaybackError on mismatch, PlaybackError when missing); cancel is sticky across the pre-spawn window via a generation counter

espeak-ng.binary: espeak-ng (NOT FOUND: absent from the Ubuntu qualification host and from node:24-bookworm-slim)
espeak-ng.hostDigest: missing — blocked: no binary anywhere to measure; ESPEAK_SHA256_PINS is empty by design (no digest is ever invented)
espeak-ng.license: GPL-3.0 (Debian espeak-ng-data 1.52.0 copyright; separate native executable, subprocess aggregation once provisioned)
espeak-ng.invocation: espeak-ng --stdin -v <voice> -s <wpm> --stdout with narration text on stdin (explicit argv carries no text; WAV collected from stdout into a bounded 8 MB buffer, child killed on abort)
espeak-ng.runtimeEnforcement: EspeakNgEngine.synthesize verifies the digest before spawn and refuses with TtsUnsupportedError while zero pins exist (provision via ESPEAK_DIGESTS allowlist); empty/oversize text and out-of-range speed fail closed without spawning; test doubles bypass verification (production never injects a runner)

networkPosture.runtimeDownloads: none — audio helpers are preinstalled system binaries or refused when absent; no npm TTS dependency added
networkPosture.audioInTests: synthetic PCM and byte-stub WAVs only via FakeDevice, FakePort and node fixtures; no audio files written, no audio payload in events or logs (counts, ids, chunk indexes and text length only)

latencyBounds.fenceCancel: 150 ms or less from barge to reaped child on the SIGTERM path (asserted in playback and voice-loop tests against the §9 gate)
latencyBounds.sigkillEscalation: bounded 500 ms for children that ignore SIGTERM (100 ms escalation plus CI margin; exceeds the 150 ms gate for hung children only)

trustBoundary.hashThenExec: digest verified immediately before spawn, executed by path (TOCTOU inherited from the L4 arecord pattern and accepted there); ESPEAK_DIGESTS/APLAY_DIGESTS/APLAY_BIN/ESPEAK_BIN env overrides allow operator-chosen binaries and are therefore trusted operator input, recorded here
trustBoundary.narrationText: text travels on espeak stdin (never argv, never /proc cmdline); WAV bytes travel espeak-stdout to aplay-stdin with no filesystem copy; RAM buffers are dropped after close

sbom.delta: empty — L6a adds zero packages to package.json/package-lock.json; SBOM is the unchanged L3 set plus hashed system binaries

liveTtsVoice.detail: No qualified espeak-ng binary exists on the host or in the pinned image (only lib + voice data are present). The TTS entry refuses until a digest-pinned binary is provisioned; no silent fallback, no invented digest.

openMicEcho.detail: Speaker playback plus open-mic VAD may self-trigger barge-in on the loop's own narration (no AEC reference — see L4 receipt). Headset-only until a qualified AEC reference exists; key mode is unaffected.

inImageHelpers.detail: aplay/espeak-ng are absent from node:24-bookworm-slim and no lane may provision them (ad-hoc docker work is forbidden). Exact missing §8.1 items: (1) pinned image digest for node:24-bookworm-slim, (2) in-image aplay + espeak-ng digests, (3) offline execution trace inside that image, (4) network-denial log for that provisioning.
